newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - APRIL 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - APRIL 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The finance ministry is following new tactics to bolster the participation of institutional investors - primarily from pension funds but also from abroad - in the auctions of state titles. Sources say the government's economic team plans to establish primary dealers as soon as possible.

-- New share offers on the Athens Stock Exchange are drawing the attention of foreign institutional investors following a new fall in interest rates. Interest is centred on Greek telecoms organisation OTE's second share offer as well as National Bank's, Alpha Credit and Ergo Bank.

--More realistic pricing for the sale of Cretabank as well as the bank's increased branch network has boosted buyers' interest. Interest has been expressed by the Bank of Piraeus, Eurobank and a group of foreign businessmen.

--The government is planning on tightening the guidelines regarding pensioner's liimits on extra income in an effort to release jobs for the unemployed. The reform will be discussed in social dialogue between government, unions and employers, due to begin soon.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou's recent appeal to bankers for self-restraint in the deceleration of interest rates appears to have fallen on deaf ears: National Bank of Greece dropped its rates by 50 basis points on Friday following the announcement of March inflation falling to 6.0 percent.

--Charges amounting to up to 10 percent of the interest rates on credit cards were the focus of talks between the deputy development minister and the Association of Greek Banks. The ministry says there are serious discrepancies between daily interest rates and annual charges.

--Four major changes in the job market - reduced wages for young unemployed, incease in levels for mass lay-offs, a reduced working week for reduced pay and incentives for part-time positions - are the focus of dissent within the government, specifically between the national economy and labour ministries, as well as from unionists.

--The banking market's interest is focused on a generation that has learnt to live on borrowed ... money. The first generation of Greek consumers to rely on lending is the object of fierce competition by banks as the latter struggle to carve out a share of the market.
